title: IOB Calculation
body:
Since updating to version 3.3.2.1, I’ve noticed that the IOB shown on the main screen doesn’t match the one in the SMB tab. I’m not sure if this is a bug or if it’s related to a setting, but it only started happening after the update.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9bcb33f5-1b0e-4ffc-a385-163ddee87c0d)
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d4d974d1-b0ec-49ef-88a7-e029ad9eebbc)

[AndroidAPS_LOG_1757911672478.log.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22327948/AndroidAPS_LOG_1757911672478.log.zip)

AAPS 3.3.2.1
Build: 937e2bccc9-2025.09.04
Remote: https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS.git
Flavor: fullrelease

comments.body: this should not happen. what was the previous version?
could you try to revert to this version and check if the problem disappear?

I reverted the version, but the problem was the same. I have now let the IOB run at 0 (deactivated the loop for a few hours) and am observing whether it drifts apart again...

I have another idea – I was thinking about what else I changed besides updating to AAPS 3.3.2.1.

A few days ago, I switched from Lumjev to NovoRapid due to intolerance. Could this possibly be causing the problem?

@MilosKozak , I deleted AAPS completely, did a clean reinstall, and didn’t restore any old data, so I accepted the “Fallback to SMB. Not enough TDD data.” message as part of the reset.

The result: the IOB values in the Main tab and the SMB tab are now back in sync.

@MilosKozak  
One week after my reset, I now have TDD data again and can switch from SMB to dynamicISF – and lo and behold –

SMB: IOB correct on both tabs (1.71)
Dynamic ISF: Main tab 1.71, SMB tab 1.91

When I deactivate dynamicISF, both values are identical again. The loop also doesn’t always make logical decisions in dynamicISF mode. For me, it’s not a problem to keep using the SMB mode and leave dynamicISF deactivated. So, I’m playing it safe for now.
This is nice catch. Thanks. I'll investigate

I checked the code and it's OK.
Basal IOB (from TBR) calculation is affected by sensitivity detection. I checked our production phone with fine tuned settings and both IOBs are very close because autosens result and sensitivity change provided by DynISF mode are very close.
It means your DynISF settings is very off.
To check this, your average ISF provided by DynISF should be about the one you have in your profile (expecting it's correct because the alg works well for you in SMB mode)
